Apple___Apple_scab.description: Fungal disease causing olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves, fruit lesions, and premature leaf drop.
symptoms: Olive-green to velvety brown-black spots on leaf surfaces
Cracked or deformed developing fruit with corky scabs
Yellowing and premature shedding of infected foliage
organic_treatment: Apply wettable sulfur or liquid lime-sulfur during early green tip stage
Spray copper octanoate (soap fungicide) before bloom
Prune canopy vigorously to enhance airflow and sunlight penetration
chemical_treatment: Captan 50 WP or Mancozeb 75 WG protective sprays applied at pink bud stage
Myclobutanil or Difenoconazole systemic triazole fungicides if lesions appear
Rotate active ingredients every 2 sprays to prevent fungal resistance
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering spores
Select scab-resistant cultivars such as Liberty, Prima, or Enterprise
Avoid overhead irrigation; water at base during early morning

Apple___Black_rot.description: Destructive fungal infection causing circular leaf spots with purple margins (frog-eye), cankers on branches, and rotting fruit.
symptoms: Circular purple spots with tan or brown centers resembling frog eyes
Black sunken cankers on limbs and main branches
Firm brown fruit rot with concentric rings turning completely black and mummified
organic_treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides starting at silver tip bud development
Cut away infected twigs and cankers 15 cm below visible margins
Remove all mummified fruit hanging from tree branches
chemical_treatment: Apply Thiophanate-methyl combined with Captan starting from petal fall
Fludioxonil or Pyraclostrobin protective sprays during early fruit development
Spray canopy immediately after severe hail or storm damage
prevention: Sanitize pruning tools in 70% isopropyl alcohol between every cut
Burn or bury all pruned infected wood and mummified fruit
Maintain balanced tree vigor without excessive nitrogen fertilization

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Fungal disease requiring Eastern red cedar/juniper and apple trees to complete its life cycle.
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange circular spots on upper leaf surfaces
Tiny raised black dots (pycnia) within orange leaf spots
Tubular fringed fruiting structures (aecia) on the underside of leaves
organic_treatment: Apply sulfur or copper sprays when orange rust horns swell on nearby cedars
Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide weekly during rainy spring intervals
chemical_treatment: Myclobutanil (Immunox) applied from pink bud through petal fall
Mancozeb or Propiconazole applied on a 7-10 day schedule during wet spells
prevention: Remove eastern red cedar trees within 1 to 2 miles of apple orchards
Plant resistant apple varieties like Redfree, Freedom, or Williams Pride
Monitor nearby junipers in spring for gelatinous galls

Apple___healthy.description: The apple foliage displays optimal health with deep green coloration, firm turgor, and no signs of lesions or pathogens.
symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves are vibrant, clean, and intact.
organic_treatment: Maintain current balanced organic compost mulching and regular monitoring.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Continue routine inspections every 7-10 days
Maintain drip irrigation schedule and optimal soil pH (6.0 - 6.8)
Perform dormant oil spray in late winter to suppress insect eggs

Blueberry___healthy.description: Vigorous blueberry bush foliage exhibiting rich green pigment, healthy vein structure, and no signs of chlorosis or fungal blights.
symptoms: Healthy foliage with no leaf spot, scorch, or powdery residue.
organic_treatment: Maintain acidic pine needle or pine bark mulch.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Ensure soil pH remains between 4.5 and 5.2
Ensure excellent drainage and consistent soil moisture
Inspect regularly for spotted wing drosophila or blueberry maggot

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Fungal infection producing white powdery mycelial growth on young leaves, shoots, and fruit stems.
symptoms: Patches of white talcum-like powdery fungus on leaf undersides
Leaves curl upwards, become distorted and brittle
Infected fruit may become deformed, leathery, and drop prematurely
organic_treatment: Spray horticultural oil or potassium bicarbonate at 1-2% solution
Apply wettable sulfur at petal fall and shuck split (avoid if temp > 30°C)
Neem oil spray applied in early mornings
chemical_treatment: Quinoxyfen or Triflumizole applied during post-bloom canopy expansion
Trifloxystrobin or Boscalid rotation every 10-14 days during warm dry weather
prevention: Prune inner canopy to maximize sunlight penetration and reduce micro-humidity
Avoid excessive late-season nitrogen fertilizers that promote succulent growth
Ensure trees are planted with adequate spacing for wind circulation

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: Pristine cherry foliage showing deep green color, smooth surface, and strong leaf petioles.
symptoms: No disease symptoms identified. Leaves are clean and vigorous.
organic_treatment: Maintain weed-free tree base and organic mulching.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Regular scouting for leaf spot and Japanese beetles
Prune canopy during dry weather to encourage good air circulation
Apply dormant copper spray in autumn after leaf fall

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Devastating foliar disease characterized by rectangular, vein-delimited lesions that cause extensive leaf blighting.
symptoms: Narrow, rectangular, tan to grayish-brown lesions bordered by leaf veins
Lesions expand and coalesce causing complete leaf desiccation
Premature senescence of ear leaf and upper foliage reducing grain fill
organic_treatment: Biofungicide sprays based on Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma harzianum
Deep tillage of crop residue to accelerate residue decomposition
chemical_treatment: Pyraclostrobin (Headline AMP) or Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole (Quilt Xcel)
Apply fungicide between V12 and R1 (silking) when disease pressure is high
prevention: Plant corn hybrids with high resistance ratings to Gray Leaf Spot
Rotate crops with non-grasses like soybeans or alfalfa for at least 1-2 years
Manage field residue through strip-till or shredding

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Fungal pathogen that produces cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
symptoms: Oval to elongate cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture epidermal tissue releasing masses of urediniospores
Severe infections turn leaves yellow, dry out, and reduce photosynthetic capacity
organic_treatment: Apply sulfur dust or bio-fungicide formulations early in morning
Enhance plant vigor through potassium-rich organic amendments
chemical_treatment: Triazole fungicides like Tebuconazole or Propiconazole
Strobilurin fungicides (e.g. Pyraclostrobin) applied at first pustule emergence
prevention: Plant Rp-resistant gene corn hybrids
Plant early in the season to escape late summer airborne spore showers
Scout whorls and lower leaves weekly during cool, moist periods (16-25°C)

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Fungal disease causing long, elliptical, grayish-green or tan cigar-shaped lesions across leaves.
symptoms: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped lesions (2.5 to 15 cm in length)
Lesions start grayish-green and mature into tan or dark necrotic zones
Olive-gray fungal sporulation appears inside lesions during damp mornings
organic_treatment: Trichoderma viride soil application and foliar bio-protective spray
Ensure crop residue shredding and incorporation post-harvest
chemical_treatment: Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole or Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad
Apply between VT (tasseling) and R2 (blister) if lesions reach 3rd leaf below ear
prevention: Select resistant hybrids containing Ht genes (Ht1, Ht2, Ht3, or HtN)
Implement a 2-year rotation out of corn
Ensure balanced fertilization and avoid plant crowding

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Vibrant emerald corn leaf blade free of pustules, streaks, and necrosis, showing strong photosynthesis.
symptoms: Uniform green leaves with well-defined parallel venation and zero pustules.
organic_treatment: Continue side-dressing with balanced compost tea or nitrogen rich manures.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Scout canopy weekly around silking time for pests and fungal spots
Maintain optimal soil moisture during tasseling and pollination
Implement preventive soil health practices

Grape___Black_rot.description: Highly destructive grapevine disease that turns leaves spotted and berries into shriveled hard black mummies.
symptoms: Small round reddish-brown spots with dark borders on leaves
Tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) arranged in rings inside leaf spots
Berries turn brown, rot within 48 hours, and shrivel into wrinkled black mummies
organic_treatment: Copper hydroxide or Bordeaux mixture applied pre-bloom and post-bloom
Thorough removal and destruction of all mummified grape clusters from vines and soil
chemical_treatment: Mancozeb or Ziram applied from 1-inch shoot growth until 4 weeks post-bloom
Myclobutanil (Rally 40WSP) or Tebuconazole for eradication of early infections
prevention: Canopy management (shoot thinning and leaf pulling) to increase airflow
Eliminate wild Vitis grapevines nearby that harbor fungal reserves
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Complex grapevine trunk disease causing 'tiger-stripe' interveinal chlorosis on leaves and spotted berries.
symptoms: 'Tiger-striped' leaves with yellow/red halos and necrotic tissue between veins
Dark purple or black measles-like speckles across ripening fruit
Vascular necrosis and internal wood decay inside cordon or trunk
organic_treatment: Apply Trichoderma-based pruning wound sealants immediately after pruning
Gently prune dead arms back to sound healthy white wood during dormancy
chemical_treatment: No systemic chemical completely cures established Esca trunk infections
Apply wound protectant fungicides (Thiophanate-methyl) immediately after cuts
prevention: Prune late in the dormant season when pruning wound susceptibility is lowest
Disinfect shears and pruning saws with 70% alcohol or bleach between vines
Replace vines showing extensive trunk rot and collar dieback

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Foliar disease producing irregular reddish-brown necrotic spots that can lead to extensive defoliation.
symptoms: Irregular, angular reddish-brown to dark brown leaf spots
Dark felt-like fungal sporulation on lower leaf surface within spots
Premature defoliation, particularly in lower and shaded canopy zones
organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + slaked lime) spray
Neem-based botanical fungicides applied at 10-14 day intervals
chemical_treatment: Mancozeb 75 WP or Copper Oxychloride 50 WP
Carbendazim or Azoxystrobin applied when lesions first appear
prevention: Practice shoot positioning and canopy thinning to reduce humidity
Remove fallen leaves after harvest to reduce overwintering inoculum
Avoid excessive irrigation during vegetative growth

Grape___healthy.description: Healthy palmate grape leaf with vibrant green coloring, sharp margins, and zero discoloration.
symptoms: Leaves are supple, uniform in color, and completely free of spots or webbing.
organic_treatment: Maintain balanced organic vine nutrition and mulch layer.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Maintain trellis canopy management for optimal sun exposure
Monitor weekly for downy mildew, powdery mildew, and leafhoppers
Apply preventive sulfur spray during warm, dry pre-bloom periods

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Fatal bacterial disease transmitted by the Asian citrus psyllid, causing asymmetrical blotchy leaf mottle and bitter lopsided fruit.
symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy yellowing and mottling across leaf veins (not mirrored on halves)
Yellowing of individual shoots ('yellow shoot' symptom)
Small, lopsided fruit that stays green at base and tastes bitter and salty
Twig dieback and progressive tree decline
organic_treatment: Release biological control parasitoid wasps (Tamarixia radiata) against psyllids
Foliar sprays of horticultural mineral oils to deter psyllid egg-laying
Comprehensive micronutrient foliar feeding (zinc, iron, manganese) to prolong tree vigor
chemical_treatment: Intensive vector control with systemic insecticides (Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam)
Trunk injection of oxytetracycline antibiotic in certified programs where authorized
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free rootstocks and scions from enclosed nurseries
Eradicate infected trees promptly to prevent transmission to neighboring orchards
Monitor psyllid populations using yellow sticky cards year-round

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial infection causing angular water-soaked leaf spots, shot-hole effect, and deep fruit pitting.
symptoms: Small, angular, water-soaked spots that turn dark purple to black
Infected centers drop out, creating a 'shot-hole' appearance on leaves
Pitted, cracked, and gumming lesions on developing peaches
organic_treatment: Apply low-rate copper formulations (copper hydroxide) during dormancy and bloom
Use Bacillus subtilis (Serenade ASO) bio-bactericide weekly during wet spells
chemical_treatment: Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) applied at weekly intervals from petal fall to cover
Copper bactericides at very low rates to prevent foliar phytotoxicity
prevention: Plant resistant peach varieties (e.g. Candor, Clayton, Reliance, Sentinel)
Avoid sandy soil sites prone to blowing grit that abrades plant cuticles
Maintain optimal potassium and nitrogen balance to avoid lush growth

Peach___healthy.description: Lush lanceolate peach leaf with rich green color, smooth serrated borders, and zero blemishes.
symptoms: Foliage shows vibrant color, normal elongation, and no bacterial spots.
organic_treatment: Maintain balanced organic orchard floor cover.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Dormant copper spray during autumn leaf drop to protect next season's buds
Regular scouting for peach leaf curl and oriental fruit moth
Prune open-center vase shapes to maximize airflow

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease thriving in warm wet conditions causing small brown water-soaked leaf spots and defoliation.
symptoms: Small, circular to irregular water-soaked spots on leaf surfaces
Spots turn brown with yellow chlorotic halos, becoming necrotic
Extensive defoliation exposing bell peppers to severe sunscald
organic_treatment: Fixed copper sprays combined with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
Remove and destroy infected plant debris immediately upon detection
chemical_treatment: Copper hydroxide tank-mixed with Mancozeb (improves copper bioavailability)
Acibenzolar-S-methyl (Actigard) plant defense activator applied preventively
prevention: Use certified pathogen-free, hot-water treated seed
Never work or cultivate in pepper fields when foliage is wet
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation away from solanaceous vegetables

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: Healthy glossy green pepper leaf with firm structure and clear veins, indicating robust nutrition.
symptoms: Glossy, uniform leaf surfaces with no spots, wilt, or necrosis.
organic_treatment: Apply balanced calcium-magnesium and seaweed extract foliar spray.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage
Maintain soil calcium levels to prevent blossom end rot
Scout for aphids, thrips, and spider mites

Potato___Early_blight.description: Common foliar fungal disease causing dark brown spots with characteristic concentric rings (target-board pattern).
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings resembling a target board
Yellow halo surrounding mature spots
Lesions start on older lower leaves and progressively move up the plant
organic_treatment: Copper sulfate or copper octanoate applied every 7-10 days
Biofungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or Trichoderma viride
Strip severely infected lower leaves from plant base
chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil (Bravo Weather Stik) or Mancozeb protective sprays
Azoxystrobin (Quadris) or Boscalid (Endura) at first sign of target spots
prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation without potatoes, tomatoes, or eggplants
Maintain adequate nitrogen and potassium fertilization to reduce plant stress
Use certified disease-free seed tubers

Potato___Late_blight.description: Fast-moving oomycete pathogen responsible for the Irish Potato Famine; rapidly destroys foliage and rots tubers.
symptoms: Large, dark brown to purplish-black water-soaked lesions expanding rapidly
Delicate white cottony fungal growth on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Stems develop dark greasy lesions causing whole vines to collapse within days
Tubers develop dry granular reddish-brown rot extending into flesh
organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture or copper oxychloride applied preventively before rain
Destroy and bury all blighted foliage immediately to protect tubers
chemical_treatment: Mandipropamid (Revus) or Cyazofamid (Ranman) protective sprays
Metalaxyl / Mefenoxam + Mancozeb curative systemic spray during outbreaks
prevention: Plant resistant potato varieties (e.g. Defender, Sarpo Mira, Elba)
Hill up potatoes deeply with soil to prevent zoospores washing down to tubers
Destroy cull piles and eliminate volunteer potatoes in early spring

Potato___healthy.description: Vibrant, broad green potato compound leaf displaying optimal vegetative growth and turgor.
symptoms: Clean green compound leaves without target rings or water-soaked lesions.
organic_treatment: Maintain balanced organic hilling and potassium nutrition.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Regular scouting during cool, wet, overcast weather periods
Maintain soil drainage and adequate hilling depth
Avoid overhead irrigation after mid-afternoon

Raspberry___healthy.description: Vigorous serrated raspberry leaves showing healthy green top and soft silvery underside, free of rust or cane blight.
symptoms: Normal pinnate leaves, free of yellowing, rust pustules, or scorch.
organic_treatment: Apply woodchip mulch and composted manure around cane bases.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Thin primocanes annually to maintain 10-15 cm spacing for air circulation
Trellis canes off the ground to keep leaves dry
Inspect for raspberry cane borers and spider mites

Soybean___healthy.description: Robust trifoliate soybean leaves with deep green chlorophyll saturation and absence of frogeye or rust lesions.
symptoms: Clean trifoliate foliage with active photosynthesis and nodulation.
organic_treatment: Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium japonicum for nitrogen fixation.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Scout regularly between R1 and R5 growth stages for foliar diseases
Maintain standard crop rotation with corn or small grains
Ensure weed management to eliminate alternative pathogen hosts

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Very prevalent fungal disease causing white talcum-powder-like fungal patches across cucurbit leaves and stems.
symptoms: White circular powdery fungal spots on upper and lower leaf surfaces
Spots spread to cover entire leaf surface, petiole, and stem
Infected leaves turn yellow, brown, shrivel, and become brittle, reducing fruit yield
organic_treatment: Spray potassium bicarbonate (3-5 g/L) or diluted milk solution (1:9 ratio)
Neem oil (0.5-1%) or botanical horticultural oils applied early morning
Sulfur sprays applied before temperatures exceed 30°C
chemical_treatment: Myclobutanil or Triflumizole systemic fungicides
Cyflufenamid or Quinoxyfen applied preventively at first appearance
prevention: Select powdery mildew resistant squash cultivars (e.g. Success PM, Dunja)
Plant in full sun with generous spacing between squash hills
Water plants at base using drip tape rather than overhead sprinklers

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Fungal disease causing numerous small purplish spots that expand and coalesce, making the leaf look scorched by fire.
symptoms: Irregular purple-to-brown spots with dark margins on upper leaf surfaces
Spots lack the pale white centers of common leaf spot
Leaves turn brown, curl upwards at margins, and appear burned or scorched
organic_treatment: Copper-based organic fungicides applied in early spring
Clip and destroy older infected leaves after harvest during renovation
chemical_treatment: Captan 50 WP or Pyraclostrobin + Boscalid (Pristine WG)
Apply in early spring as new crown leaves begin emerging
prevention: Renovate strawberry beds annually by mowing old foliage after harvest
Ensure beds are well-drained and avoid excessive spring nitrogen
Plant certified disease-free strawberry plugs

Strawberry___healthy.description: Vibrant trifoliate strawberry foliage with rich green color, serrated edges, and strong crowns.
symptoms: Crisp, green leaves with no purple spots, scorch, or powdery fungal growth.
organic_treatment: Apply clean straw mulch under developing fruit and foliage.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Keep berries and leaves elevated above wet bare soil with straw
Drip irrigate to minimize leaf wetness duration
Scout for two-spotted spider mites and gray mold (Botrytis)

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing dark, water-soaked, greasy spots on leaves, stems, and scabby spots on fruit.
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked circular spots (under 3 mm) on foliage
Spots may be surrounded by a narrow yellow halo
Centers become dry and tear out; extensive infection causes severe defoliation
Fruit exhibits small, raised, black blister-like scabs
organic_treatment: Spray copper hydroxide tank-mixed with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
Hydrogen dioxide / peracetic acid sanitizing sprays
chemical_treatment: Copper bactericide mixed with Mancozeb to enhance copper efficacy
Acibenzolar-S-methyl (Actigard) systemic acquired resistance inducer
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 25 min)
Do not work in tomato patches when plants are damp with rain or dew
Rotate tomato fields with corn, beans, or brassicas for 2+ years

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Destructive fungal pathogen causing prominent concentric rings (target spots) that start on lower leaves and move upward.
symptoms: Brown-to-black spots with distinct concentric rings (target pattern)
Leaves turn yellow around the lesions and drop off prematurely
Stem lesions (collar rot) develop at the soil line on young transplants
Sunken, leathery dark lesions on fruit near the stem end
organic_treatment: Apply copper octanoate or copper sulfate at 7-10 day intervals
Foliar spray with Bacillus subtilis biofungicide
Prune bottom 30 cm of foliage to prevent soil splash
chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin applied preventively
Difenoconazole + Cyprodinil (Inspire Super) for systemic control
prevention: Stake or cage plants and mulch soil heavily with straw or plastic film
Avoid overhead irrigation; use drip lines at the soil level
Practice 3-year crop rotation away from all nightshades

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Fast-acting, catastrophic disease that can destroy an entire tomato crop within days during cool, wet weather.
symptoms: Large, irregular, pale to dark water-soaked lesions that turn dark brown
White fungal-like fuzzy growth on the underside of leaves during high humidity
Brown to black greasy lesions on petioles and main stems
Large, firm, bumpy golden-brown lesions on green fruit
organic_treatment: Preventive copper sprays before wet overcast conditions set in
Bag and destroy infected plants immediately—never compost late blight vines
chemical_treatment: Mandipropamid (Revus), Cyazofamid (Ranman), or Fluopicolide (Presidio)
Apply immediately upon late blight weather alert warnings
prevention: Plant resistant tomato varieties (e.g. Mountain Magic, Defiant, Plum Regal)
Ensure wide plant spacing (at least 60-90 cm) for rapid drying of foliage
Destroy volunteer tomato plants and potato cull piles nearby

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Fungal disease common in high tunnels and greenhouses with high humidity (>85%), causing yellow leaf spots with olive mold.
symptoms: Pale green or pale yellow spots with indefinite margins on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to velvety brown mold growth on the corresponding lower surface
Leaves turn yellow, curl, wither, and drop off prematurely
organic_treatment: Copper hydroxide or liquid copper spray applied to lower leaf surfaces
Biofungicides like Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or Streptomyces lydicus
chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Difenoconazole
Ensure thorough coverage of both upper and lower leaf surfaces
prevention: Increase greenhouse ventilation with exhaust fans and horizontal airflow
Keep relative humidity below 80% through night heating and venting
Prune suckers and lower leaves to maximize air movement through the canopy

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Prolific fungal leaf spot disease causing defoliation from the base upward, exposing tomatoes to sunscald.
symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1.5 - 3 mm) with dark brown margins and gray/tan centers
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) clearly visible in center of each spot
Heavily infected leaves turn completely yellow, wither, and drop
organic_treatment: Copper soap (copper octanoate) applied at 7-day intervals
Remove and discard severely infected bottom leaves
chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil (Bravo) or Mancozeb protective sprays starting at transplanting
Pyraclostrobin (Cabrio) or Azoxystrobin at symptom emergence
prevention: Apply thick organic mulch (straw or wood shavings) to block fungal spore splash
Drip irrigate only; do not wet tomato leaves
Rake and destroy all plant debris at the end of every season

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Microscopic sap-feeding arachnid pests that pierce plant cells, causing yellow stippling and fine silken webbing.
symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling (speckling) across upper leaf surfaces
Fine silken webbing on leaf undersides, growing tips, and flower clusters
Leaves turn bronze or yellow, dry up, and drop during hot, dry weather
organic_treatment: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis or Neoseiulus californicus)
Spray insecticidal soap or 1% neem oil, thoroughly coating leaf undersides
Spray cold water under leaves with high pressure to knock mites off
chemical_treatment: Abamectin (Agri-Mek) or Bifenazate (Acramite) miticides
Spiromesifen (Oberon) targeting mite eggs and nymphs
prevention: Keep plants adequately watered; spider mites thrive on drought-stressed plants
Keep garden borders weed-free to eliminate alternative mite reservoirs
Avoid broad-spectrum pyrethroid insecticides that kill beneficial predatory insects

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Fungal disease favored by warm, humid environments causing circular lesions with pale brown centers and concentric rings.
symptoms: Small, pinpoint, water-soaked spots that enlarge into circular brown lesions
Lesions feature concentric rings with light brown centers and dark borders
Leaf yellowing around spots followed by leaf drop
Fruit develops circular, sunken, pitted lesions
organic_treatment: Copper hydroxide spray applied at weekly intervals during rainy periods
Biofungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole, or Boscalid + Pyraclostrobin
Rotate fungicides from different FRAC groups to prevent resistance
prevention: Ensure adequate spacing between plants to reduce canopy humidity
Avoid overhead irrigation; water early in the morning
Remove and destroy all crop residues after harvest

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Devastating viral disease transmitted by the silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci); causes dramatic stunting and leaf cupping.
symptoms: Severe upward and inward cupping (curling) of leaf margins
Interveinal chlorosis and yellowing of young leaves
Pronounced plant stunting with shortened internodes creating a bushy appearance
Complete flower drop resulting in zero or severely reduced fruit set
organic_treatment: Hang yellow sticky cards to capture and monitor whiteflies
Spray insecticidal soap, neem oil, or horticultural oil on leaf undersides
Install 50-mesh insect-proof netting over greenhouse vents
chemical_treatment: No chemical can cure viral infection once the plant is infected
Control whitefly vectors using systemic insecticides (Imidacloprid, Dinotefuran, Cyantraniliprole)
prevention: Plant TYLCV-resistant tomato hybrids (e.g. Tygress, Grand Slam, Charger)
Roguing: immediately pull and destroy infected plants in sealed plastic bags
Implement a 2-month host-free period between planting seasons

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Extremely stable, easily mechanically transmitted virus causing mottled, distorted, shoestring-like leaves and uneven fruit ripening.
symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves
Leaf distortion, blistering, and 'shoestring' narrowing of leaflets
Stunted plant growth and reduced vigor
Fruit may display internal browning and uneven ripening with yellow patches
organic_treatment: No chemical or organic cure exists for virus-infected plants
Soak hands and pruning shears in non-fat dry milk solution (20%) or trisodium phosphate (TSP) to deactivate viral particles
chemical_treatment: No viricides exist for field crops. Focus completely on prevention and hygiene
prevention: Select ToMV-resistant cultivars (marked with 'T' or 'ToMV')
Wash hands thoroughly with soap before handling tomatoes; do not use tobacco near plants
Carefully rogue out and destroy any plants showing mosaic symptoms

Tomato___healthy.description: Pristine tomato compound foliage exhibiting rich chlorophyll green, vigorous pubescence, and strong leaf petioles.
symptoms: Vigorous, dark green foliage free of spots, mosaic, or leaf curl.
organic_treatment: Maintain regular weekly calcium and seaweed extract foliar feedings.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required.
prevention: Maintain consistent soil moisture to prevent blossom end rot
Mulch base of plants and maintain 60 cm staking/trellising
Scout weekly for early blight, hornworms, and whiteflies
